ScanFocus.name: Repository-wide baseline source security scan

included: All application source and documentation files in the current Codebase folder
excluded: External database infrastructure unless represented in source or docs
ThreatForge frontend/dashboard code from the referenced chat

ScanFocus.assessmentObjective: Confirm which plausible threats have complete source-backed paths, identify actual controls and counterevidence, and check for additional security-relevant implementation not captured in the existing threat model.
ScanFocus.whyThisScope: The application is a compact single-file Flask app with supporting manifests and docs. A repository-wide standard pass is small enough to be comprehensive and avoids missing startup or documentation-driven exposure paths.
requiredPrerequisites: Read-only access to current Codebase folder
limitations: Cannot prove exploitability for shell/parser/JWT/database behavior without runtime validation.
Cannot determine production blast radius without deployment details.

ScanFocus.name: Execution and interpreter exploitability review

included: Attack-path feasibility from unauthenticated HTTP input to pickle, os.popen, eval, and render_template_string
Preconditions for process compromise and server-side interpretation
Available in-process objects and controls visible in source
excluded: Payload development against a running process

ScanFocus.assessmentObjective: Determine whether route-level execution threats are reachable and what concrete preconditions are needed for exploitation.
ScanFocus.whyThisScope: Threat relationships TR001 and TR002 show shared process-execution assets across T002/T003/T006, while T001 shares the cookie boundary with T008. These are the highest-impact paths and deserve focused exploitability reasoning before dynamic testing.
expectedCoverage: Precondition list suitable for safe runtime validation planning
requiredPrerequisites: No runtime environment required for this planning/review focus
limitations: Can establish source-backed exploitability hypotheses but cannot confirm shell behavior, template object reachability, or pickle payload behavior without runtime validation.

ScanFocus.name: Parser, crypto, and JWT exploitability review

included: JWT None and HS256 branch acceptance requirements
Use of public JWKS data in token forgery hypotheses
excluded: Sending chosen ciphertexts or JWTs to a running service

ScanFocus.assessmentObjective: Establish whether parser, decryption, and JWT threats have coherent attack paths and define the exact runtime questions that remain.
ScanFocus.whyThisScope: T004, T005, and T008 depend heavily on library/runtime behavior. A focused exploitability review clarifies whether runtime validation should target entity resolution, response-oracle behavior, token construction, or all three.
requiredPrerequisites: Dependency version context from SF-06 if exact library behavior is needed
limitations: Cannot confirm oracle timing/error distinguishability or JWT parser acceptance without runtime requests.
Cannot determine lxml/libxml2 behavior precisely without installed version details.

ScanFocus.name: Controlled local runtime validation of HTTP attack surfaces

included: Default SQLite mode unless separate DB validation is selected
excluded: Testing against production or shared systems
Persistence, lateral movement, or destructive commands
External network callbacks unless explicitly approved in a lab

ScanFocus.assessmentObjective: Validate which plausible attack paths actually manifest in a safe local environment and collect behavioral evidence for triage.
ScanFocus.whyThisScope: The threat model repeatedly marks runtime behavior as uncertain. Dynamic validation is needed to determine shell behavior, XML parser resolution, padding oracle response signal, JWT branch acceptance, and database-driver-specific behavior.
expectedCoverage: Basic denial-of-service risk indicators without destructive testing
limitations: Default local behavior may not match production.
Some tests require careful payload constraints to avoid destructive effects.
External callback behavior should remain out of scope unless a safe callback target is approved.

ScanFocus.name: Database backend validation for SQL and startup authority

excluded: Destructive schema or data changes unless explicitly approved in a disposable database

ScanFocus.assessmentObjective: Determine whether T007 is exploitable against the selected backend and how T009 startup configuration changes database impact.
ScanFocus.whyThisScope: The threat model identifies SQL manipulation as backend-dependent. The application supports five database modes, so validation must be scoped to the actual backend or clearly marked as conditional.
expectedCoverage: Database privilege and data exposure boundaries
Difference between local lab impact and external DB impact
requiredPrerequisites: Agreement on destructive versus read-only test limits
limitations: Without a selected external backend, results only apply to default SQLite.
Driver and server versions can materially change statement behavior.

ScanFocus.name: Dependency and supply-chain review

included: Known advisories relevant to declared package names and supported version ranges
Security-sensitive dependency behavior relevant to route threats
excluded: Runtime environment packages not represented in a lockfile or installed package list
Transitive dependency certainty without resolved environment data
Network-based dependency fetch unless separately authorized

ScanFocus.assessmentObjective: Identify dependency advisories, unsafe lower bounds, and version ambiguity that may influence parser, JWT, crypto, and framework behavior.
ScanFocus.whyThisScope: ApplicationIntelligence records lower-bound requirements and no lockfile. Threats T004, T005, T007, and T008 depend partly on library behavior, so dependency review is needed before final exploitability conclusions.
expectedCoverage: Inputs needed for reproducible runtime validation
requiredPrerequisites: Optional: installed package inventory or lockfile for exact-version assessment
Network or advisory database access if performing live advisory lookup
limitations: With only lower-bound requirements, exact installed-version risk cannot be finalized.
Optional database dependencies may not be installed in the actual runtime.
